newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SOCCER-MAKESHIFT HUNGARY ANXIOUS TO AVOID ANOTHER EXIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAKESHIFT HUNGARY ANXIOUS TO AVOID ANOTHER EXIT.

text.p: Hungary and Switzerland are aiming to put their World Cup campaigns back on track in their group three qualifier on Wednesday.
Defeat would almost certainly extend the Hungarians' unenviable record of failing to qualify for every major competition since 1986.
A result is just as vital for the fourth-placed Swiss, one point behind their opponents with a game in hand.

Hungarian coach Janos Csank has selection problems. First choice sweeper Emil Lorincz is out injured and Janos Banfi was left out of the squad after Belgian club Eendracht Aalst refused to release him for the pre-match training camp.
Ujpest's Vilmos Sebok was drafted in but picked up an injury in his side's UEFA Cup match last week.
That leaves Csank with a choice of playing inexperienced youngster Attila Dragoner from Ferencvaros or moving Anderlecht midfielder Florian Urban into a deeper role.
"I'll be choosing between Dragoner and Urban," said Csank, "We'll find a solution."
In a bid to win the midfield battle, Csank may also turn to Peter Lipcsei, who has not started an international game in more than 18 months.
Switzerland's own injury problems worsened when top striker Kubilay Tuerkyilmaz tore a thigh muscle in a warm-up game.
Tuerkyilmaz, who scored the only goal of the match against Hungary in April, is a doubtful starter, while Sion striker Marco Grassi has already pulled out with a foot injury.
The absences could leave the Swiss short of fire-power as the substitute strike pair of Patrick de Napoli and Sebastien Zambas have just one cap between them.
Top playmaker Ciriaco Sforza and fellow midfielder Murat Yakin have regained fitness and are available.
